title: Debounce presubmit triggers and introduce incremental linter cache
author: Aisha Banerjee
description: Motivation: presubmit pipelines have become noisy and slow due to immediate CI triggers on rapid developer pushes and many dependency-chore PRs. This PR implements a debounce layer for push/branch events so rapid successive commits within a short window are coalesced into a single presubmit run, and adds an incremental linter cache keyed by tool version + file globs to avoid re-linting unmodified packages. We also add a small dependency-whitelist mechanism so authorized chore PRs (approved dep bumps from our depbot pipeline) can take a lightweight validation path rather than the full heavy presubmit. The changeset is intentionally incremental: 1) an event debounce service that runs as a lightweight GitHub Actions composite step and a small Go shim to translate webhooks into coalesced workflow_dispatch events 2) a disk-backed incremental linter cache used by existing golangci-lint and eslint invocations with fallthrough to fresh lint runs when cache versioning mismatches 3) a dep-whitelist JSON manifest and workflow guard to route chore PRs to a lightweight pipeline 4) small release-hook adjustment to avoid firing release workflows for chore-only merges. Checklist: - [x] add debounce composite action + shim - [x] implement incremental lint cache and integrate with existing lint jobs - [x] add dep-whitelist manifest + lightweight workflow - [x] updates to docs and contributing guide - [x] smoke run on staging repository Rollout plan: deploy debounce action to canary org for 48h, monitor presubmit queue and merge latency, then flip org-level flag for full rollout. If regressions observed rollback by removing webhook-forwarding secret and revert action inputs. Related: ENG-2145 tracks presubmit cost reduction, ENG-2210 tracks dep-routing. Notes: debouncing window defaults to 90s (configurable per-repo) to balance feedback latency and unnecessary runs. The linter cache is safe by versioning linter tool versions and cache schema; any mismatch triggers a cold lint. This PR focuses on developer experience and CI cost; it does not change production runtime or model-serving behavior.

review_thread: Tomás Müller: Can we add unit tests for the debounce shim and a simple e2e smoke that simulates three rapid pushes? Please also document the window config default.
Aisha Banerjee: Added a small harness under tools/ci/webhook-debounce/testdata and a scripted smoke in docs. The window default is 90s and configurable via action input. See docs/ci/README.md.
Bradley Chen: The lint cache looks good but we should ensure cache invalidation is deterministic when toolchain updates land. Suggest adding a cache-schema version file to the cache key.
Aisha Banerjee: Added cache-schema versioning and included golangci-lint and eslint versions in the key. Also added a fallback to full lint run if the cache read fails.
Sofia Patel: Verified e2e on canary org, presubmit runs reduced 42% on average for burst pushes. LGTM pending CI.
CI Bot: Build passed on push, tests passed, lint job used cache hit rate 76%.
release_notes: Adds CI debounce to reduce redundant presubmit runs, introduces incremental lint caching for faster feedback, and adds a dependency whitelist to route approved chore PRs to a lightweight validation pipeline. No runtime changes.
testing_instructions: 1) Deploy tools/ci/webhook-debounce to a test repo and configure webhook-secret; push three commits within 30s and verify a single presubmit run is kicked. 2) Create a sample chore PR that only bumps dev deps and add it to ci/dep-whitelist.json; verify it executes lightweight-presubmit.yml instead of presubmit.yml. 3) Change a Go file and run the lint pipeline twice; second run should hit the cache if tool versions unchanged. Logs for cache hit/miss are written to /tmp/presubmit-cache-logs during local runs.
